automotive-ev-battery.title: Canada invests billions in charging infrastructure and grid upgrades
automotive-ev-battery.summary: The Canadian government is investing over $634 million to expand electric vehicle charging infrastructure, roughly doubling the existing 50,000 chargers currently supported. The investment is part of a broader national electricity strategy committing over $50 billion to double Canada's grid capacity by 2050.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Nevoya seals multi-year deal with Meta to deploy 25 electric trucks between California and Arizona
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Electric truckload carrier startup Nevoya has announced a multi-year commercial agreement with Meta to deploy 25 Class 8 battery-electric trucks on Interstate 10 between San Bernardino, California and Phoenix, Arizona. The deal represents a significant adoption of electric commercial vehicles by a major technology company.

automotive-ev-battery.title: $20K Nissan NX7 PHEV goes on sale with nearly 200 miles of electric range
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Dongfeng Nissan has opened pre-orders for its new NX7 plug-in hybrid vehicle, featuring up to 198 miles of all-electric range from a 40 kWh lithium iron phosphate battery at a starting price of $20,000. The vehicle represents an affordable entry point into electrified personal transportation.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Huawei set to challenge Tesla Powerwall with new, 20 kW home battery
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Huawei has unveiled a new home battery system featuring 20 kW capacity, silicon carbide technology, and AI-powered energy management capabilities to compete with Tesla's Powerwall. The modular storage solution is designed to provide residential backup power during outages.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Tesla Starts Selling Cybercab — $30,000*
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Tesla has officially launched sales of its Cybercab robotaxi, priced starting at $29,900 for select customers. The vehicle requires a $299 monthly autonomy subscription and operates only within Tesla's Robotaxi service areas in Texas and Florida.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Zoox Launches Robotaxis in Atlanta
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Zoox has expanded its autonomous robotaxi service to Atlanta, initially focusing on the Northwest region near Atlantic Station, Woodward, and Home Park before planned expansion throughout the city. The expansion continues the company's rollout following recent service launches in Las Vegas.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Zoox Expands Robotaxi Service in Las Vegas
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Zoox has expanded its commercial robotaxi operations in Las Vegas beyond the Strip, extending service into Downtown and the Arts District. The expansion demonstrates growing commercial viability of autonomous vehicle services in major metropolitan areas.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Check your ego at the door: Stellantis' new electric dolly turns ANY car into a tow rig
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Stellantis has patented an AI-powered electric tow dolly that can convert virtually any vehicle into a capable towing vehicle without requiring a dedicated truck. The technology represents an innovative approach to reducing consumer dependence on traditional gas-powered pickup trucks.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Legal proceedings should establish whether the BYD Ti7 is a Copy of JLR's Defender
automotive-ev-battery.summary: British automaker Jaguar Land Rover has initiated legal action against Chinese competitor BYD alleging patent infringement, with court authorities seizing digital documents from BYD offices in the Netherlands in August. A court has since ruled the seizure action unnecessary and ordered the destruction of seized data.

automotive-ev-battery.title: I finally got a USB-C charging e-bike, and it costs 75% less than Rivian's bike
automotive-ev-battery.summary: An electric bike manufacturer has launched a USB-C charging model at a significantly lower price point than premium alternatives like Rivian's offering. The adoption of USB-C charging represents an industry shift toward standardized, convenient charging across consumer electronics.

finance-markets.title: Trump Media group stares down $1bn debt crunch as bitcoin bet fades
finance-markets.summary: Trump Media, the parent company of Truth Social, faces a significant financial crisis with approximately $1 billion in debt obligations coming due as share prices and cryptocurrency valuations have declined sharply. The company may be forced to pursue asset sales or secure costly new financing to navigate the debt crunch.

finance-markets.title: Nvidia board urged to consider 'potential return of Jensen Huang' by two major investors
finance-markets.summary: Two major Nvidia shareholders collectively holding $2.13 billion in stock have urged the board to consider reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO following his recent resignation. The investor push suggests ongoing turbulence regarding leadership direction at the semiconductor giant.

finance-markets.title: Nvidia exposed to possible lawsuits after Jensen Huang's downfall
finance-markets.summary: Nvidia faces potential legal liability exposure following Jensen Huang's departure, as the company lacks comprehensive insurance coverage for damages resulting from executive misconduct. This creates financial and reputational risks for the chip manufacturer during a period of leadership uncertainty.

finance-markets.title: Passengers face widespread disruption after US air traffic control outage
finance-markets.summary: A nationwide FAA system failure resulted in thousands of flight delays and cancellations, triggering political blame-shifting regarding responsibility for maintaining critical aviation infrastructure. The outage highlighted systemic vulnerabilities in America's air traffic control network.

finance-markets.title: Nationwide ground stop followed contractor upgrade to L3Harris telecommunication system: DOT's Duffy
finance-markets.summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy attributed the FAA ground stop to an update to an older L3Harris Technologies communication system, revealing the infrastructure vulnerabilities underlying critical national aviation operations. The incident underscores the need for modernization of aging systems managing air traffic control.

finance-markets.title: US air travel chaos exposes system held together by 'string and duct tape'
finance-markets.summary: Experts warn that decades of bipartisan neglect have left America's aviation infrastructure critically degraded and inadequate for current demand. The recent air traffic control failures illustrate the urgent need for substantial investment in modernizing the nation's aviation systems.

finance-markets.title: Juicy 6% Yields Gain Appeal After Nvidia Drama: Credit Weekly
finance-markets.summary: US corporate bond markets have rallied recently, with attractive six-percent yields drawing investors seeking refuge from equity market turbulence amid Nvidia-related disruptions. The credit market strength reflects a strategic rotation toward fixed-income assets among portfolio managers.

finance-markets.title: Bessent, Lutnick Clash Over Nvidia China Curbs
finance-markets.summary: Tensions within the Trump administration have surfaced regarding restrictions on advanced Nvidia chip exports to China, with disagreements between Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent over technology export policy. The dispute reflects broader national security concerns regarding US technology competition with China.

finance-markets.title: The world according to China
finance-markets.summary: China's hosting of the Apec summit in Shenzhen demonstrates Beijing's strategic ambitions to reshape the global economic and political order according to its own interests and priorities. The gathering provides a platform for China to advance its vision of regional and global governance structures.

finance-markets.title: How China's Intelligence Operations Target Tech
finance-markets.summary: A former CIA counterintelligence analyst explains how China's Ministry of State Security leverages business and personal relationships to gather intelligence within the technology sector and potentially influence strategic decision-making. The briefing highlights the expanding espionage capabilities of Chinese intelligence agencies, particularly regarding AI and advanced technologies.

science-space.title: 'Now everything changes': SpaceX catches Starship upper stage for 1st time ever
science-space.summary: SpaceX achieved a historic milestone on November 14 by successfully catching the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time, marking a significant advancement in the vehicle's development. This breakthrough capture could substantially accelerate the timeline for achieving full reusability and operational capability of the world's most powerful rocket system.

science-space.title: A giant icy world hiding beyond Pluto could be our sixth dwarf planet
science-space.summary: Astronomers have discovered a potentially massive dwarf planet designated 2026 ED138 beyond Pluto in one of the sky's most crowded regions, potentially expanding the official roster of solar system dwarf planets. The discovery suggests additional undiscovered worlds may exist in the distant outer solar system beyond Neptune.

science-space.title: Stanford scientists discover hidden brain signals that predict Alzheimer's years before symptoms
science-space.summary: Stanford researchers have identified hidden patterns of brain activity that can predict Alzheimer's disease risk years before cognitive symptoms emerge, potentially providing earlier detection than conventional biomarkers. The study also revealed brain activity patterns associated with natural resistance to aging, opening new avenues for preventive therapeutic development.

science-space.title: Why did Starship Flight 15 booster abort 'chopsticks' landing catch? SpaceX still investigating
science-space.summary: SpaceX is investigating why the Starship Flight 15 test on November 13 aborted the first of two planned booster landings during the 'chopsticks' catch attempt. The investigation into this technical failure will provide critical insights for future test flights as the company works toward perfecting reusability systems.

science-space.title: Yale scientists reveal what really slows aging and what doesn't
science-space.summary: Yale researchers analyzed 51 studies to determine that prescription drugs, healthy diets, and exercise demonstrably slow biological aging, while popular anti-aging supplements prove largely ineffective. Though the research confirms biological aging can be slowed through proven interventions, questions remain about whether these cellular changes translate to extended human lifespan.

science-space.title: A new fiber supplement could help millions suffering from irritable bowel syndrome
science-space.summary: Scientists have developed a specialized fiber supplement that improves gut health in irritable bowel syndrome patients while avoiding common side effects like bloating and pain. The supplement also reduced gut-related anxiety and produced rapid changes in gut bacterial composition, potentially offering a new therapeutic approach for IBS management.

science-space.title: Scientists discover a surprisingly simple way to turn coffee waste into fuel
science-space.summary: Researchers have developed an efficient method to convert used coffee grounds into biodiesel while preserving residual material for additional renewable fuels and valuable chemicals. The process could repurpose millions of tons of global coffee waste into a sustainable energy resource, addressing both waste management and renewable energy challenges.

science-space.title: See Jupiter and Mars make a spectacular close approach overnight Nov. 15-16
science-space.summary: Jupiter and Mars will pass within approximately one degree of each other on the night of November 15-16, creating a notable celestial viewing opportunity. This close planetary conjunction provides an excellent occasion for skywatchers to observe both gas and terrestrial planets in proximity.

science-space.title: Scientists find a simple daily routine linked to less pain and depression
science-space.summary: University of Missouri researchers found that older adults maintaining consistent daily schedules for sleep, eating, and activities reported reduced physical pain and fewer depressive symptoms, even among those with insomnia. The findings suggest that regulating the body's internal circadian clock through routine may have significant impacts on pain perception and mental health.

science-space.title: APOD: 2026 November 13 – NGC 206 and the Star Clouds of Andromeda
science-space.summary: NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day features NGC 206, a notable star cluster within the Andromeda Galaxy, accompanied by professional astronomical explanation of its significance. The image highlights the stellar formations and structures within our galactic neighbor.

world-news.title: US has floated Ukraine ceding Donbas for Nato membership, Zelensky says
world-news.summary: Ukrainian President Zelensky claims the US has proposed Ukraine cede the Donbas region in exchange for NATO membership, a significant shift in diplomatic positioning on the Russia-Ukraine conflict. The US has not officially confirmed the comments, with officials stating that multiple proposals remain under discussion.

world-news.title: Trump, Putin and Xi plan historic joint meeting in China next week, White House says
world-news.summary: The White House announces an unprecedented trilateral summit between US President Trump, Russian President Putin, and Chinese President Xi scheduled for the following week to discuss nuclear weapons reduction. This represents a major diplomatic development with implications for global geopolitical realignment.

world-news.title: Iran war live: Saudi-led coalition strikes down 3 drones in as many hours
world-news.summary: The Saudi-led coalition conducted multiple interceptions of Houthi drones over the Red Sea region, with Bahrain issuing potential danger alerts amid escalating military tensions. The incidents underscore ongoing regional instability and proxy conflict dynamics in the Middle East.

world-news.title: Saudi-led coalition intercepts two missiles, two drones in Riyadh
world-news.summary: The Saudi-led coalition intercepted multiple airborne threats targeting Riyadh as fighting intensifies in Yemen's Marib and al-Jawf regions, with UN agencies reporting over 340,000 Yemeni civilians displaced since August. The escalation highlights the humanitarian crisis and regional military dimensions of the Yemen conflict.

world-news.title: Israeli air strike kills senior Hamas commander in Gaza
world-news.summary: An Israeli air strike in Khan Younis killed Samir Abu Younis, a senior Hamas commander of the Rafah brigade, marking a significant development in ongoing Gaza operations. Hamas confirmed the death, underscoring the escalating military campaign targeting militant leadership.

world-news.title: Iraq PM sacks nine officials over oil smuggling in pro-Iran stronghold
world-news.summary: Iraq's Prime Minister dismissed nine officials following an investigation that uncovered illegal oil refineries and smuggling operations in a region controlled by the Iran-aligned militia Kataib Hezbollah. The purge reflects efforts to combat corruption and illicit financial flows in strategically significant sectors.

world-news.title: Hungarian authorities uncover $20m during probe of Orbán-era minister
world-news.summary: Hungarian authorities seized $20 million during an investigation into an official from the previous Orbán government, part of Prime Minister Péter Magyar's promised anti-corruption campaign following his April election victory. The discovery signals a potential shift in governance and accountability within Hungary.

world-news.title: Italy fines Meta €805m over accessing users' photos
world-news.summary: Italian regulators fined Meta 805 million euros for allegedly accessing and utilizing photos of 20 million users without informed consent, representing a significant data privacy enforcement action by the EU. The penalty underscores heightened regulatory scrutiny of tech giants' data handling practices in Europe.

world-news.title: Arrested generals and a threatened VP: President's son fuels Ugandan succession fever
world-news.summary: Uganda faces political instability as a 52-year-old general with close ties to the president fuels succession speculation through provocative social media posts and military threats, leading to arrests of senior military figures. The situation raises concerns about institutional stability and governance in the East African nation.

world-news.title: Netanyahu sends plea to Eisenkot for unity government
world-news.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu publicly appealed to opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form a unity government, signaling political efforts to consolidate governing coalitions during a period of regional military tensions. The development reflects ongoing Israeli political dynamics amid security concerns.

tech-ai.title: Where was Nvidia's security team?
tech-ai.summary: Nvidia's security chief departed in August amid reports that CEO Jensen Huang has stepped down over relationships, including one with an executive at a company suspected of funneling chips to China. A former intelligence officer criticized corporate security teams for being poorly equipped to detect such breaches, highlighting significant vulnerabilities in corporate oversight at the world's most valuable chipmaker.

tech-ai.title: Asian governments react to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's exit
tech-ai.summary: Asian governments are responding to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure by moving to secure chip supply commitments and monitoring impacts on local AI projects. The reactions underscore the geopolitical significance of leadership changes at the semiconductor industry's most critical company.

tech-ai.title: Elon Musk, other tech execs sign petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang
tech-ai.summary: A petition signed by Elon Musk and other tech executives has accumulated over 115,000 signatures calling for Nvidia to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang. The public show of support from industry leaders underscores the significance of Huang's leadership to the tech sector amid his unexpected departure.

tech-ai.title: Watch SpaceX successfully execute the first 'chopstick' catch of Starship
tech-ai.summary: SpaceX has successfully performed the first 'chopstick' catch of a Starship vehicle using its 'Mechazilla' launch and catch tower, a major milestone in the company's reusable rocket program. While SpaceX has previously executed the maneuver on boosters, this marks the first successful application to the Starship vehicle itself.

tech-ai.title: Work to replace old copper wire led to the FAA's ground stop
tech-ai.summary: The FAA's nationwide ground stop on Friday was caused by routine maintenance work replacing outdated copper wire with fiber optic lines at a remote FAA facility, according to Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy. The incident disrupted air traffic across the United States for over four hours before operations resumed.

tech-ai.title: Tesla opens Cybercab pre-orders 'for personal use,' with geo restrictions and a $299 monthly fee
tech-ai.summary: Tesla has opened pre-orders for its autonomous Cybercab at $29,990 with a mandatory $299 monthly autonomy subscription, though availability is restricted to areas where Tesla's Robotaxi service currently operates. Even Tesla CEO Elon Musk acknowledged the subscription fee is "too high," raising questions about the pricing strategy.

tech-ai.title: The AI graveyard: a running list of projects and startups that didn't make it
tech-ai.summary: TechCrunch has compiled a comprehensive list of AI projects and startups that have failed to deliver on their promises or have been abandoned entirely. The article examines notable failures including Apple's repeatedly delayed Siri AI and OpenAI's troubled "super app" launch, offering insights into the challenges facing AI development.

tech-ai.title: The OpenAI board member who fired Sam Altman says we still can't trust AI CEOs
tech-ai.summary: Helen Toner, the Georgetown University executive who was a key board member in the decision to fire OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, discusses ongoing concerns about AI company leadership and governance. The interview explores the November 2023 incident known as "the blip" and broader questions about accountability in the AI industry.

tech-ai.title: Jensen Huang and the decline of the visionary showman founder CEO
tech-ai.summary: An analysis of Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia reflects on the changing role of charismatic technology founder CEOs in an era of increased scrutiny and governance challenges. The piece examines how corporate leadership is evolving as companies face greater oversight and accountability demands.

tech-ai.title: Transportation secretary blames 'routine' equipment upgrade for grounding flights nationwide
tech-ai.summary: FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford characterized the nationwide flight groundings as resulting from routine equipment maintenance and stated there is "zero evidence of anything AI-related" in the incident. The clarification addresses early speculation about potential technological failures behind the massive disruption.

cybersecurity.title: Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today
cybersecurity.summary: Nearly 70 percent of websites are vulnerable to a pair of critical PHP vulnerabilities that allow attackers to seize full control of affected servers. Working exploits for these flaws are already being actively exploited in the wild, likely causing widespread service disruptions.

cybersecurity.title: Who Runs the Ransomware Group Qilin?
cybersecurity.summary: Qilin has become the world's most active ransomware affiliate program, claiming at least 365 victim organizations in the past three months. Operational security mistakes by the group's administrator have revealed evidence linking the operation to a 36-year-old man in St. Petersburg, Russia.

cybersecurity.title: US Disrupts North Korean Campaign Behind $400 Million Crypto Theft
cybersecurity.summary: The U.S. government has disrupted a North Korean social engineering campaign called 'FaceStealer' responsible for stealing over $400 million in cryptocurrency. The operation relied on sophisticated social engineering tactics to compromise victims' accounts and assets.

cybersecurity.title: Tech Firms Dismantle Botnet That Turned 1.3M TV Boxes Into Proxies
cybersecurity.summary: Google and industry partners dismantled a botnet consisting of over 1.3 million compromised Android TV set-top boxes that were secretly used as rental proxies and for advertising fraud. The takedown is expected to sever access to an additional 10 million compromised IoT devices including healthcare equipment.

cybersecurity.title: Trezor Confirms Crypto-Stealing Implants in Three Wallets, Releases Fix
cybersecurity.summary: Trezor confirmed that three hardware wallets sold through a Southeast Asian reseller contained malicious hardware implants designed to steal wallet recovery phrases. The compromised devices transmitted stolen credentials over cellular networks, exposing users to complete loss of cryptocurrency assets.

cybersecurity.title: Want to Rent an Internet Address at the White House?
cybersecurity.summary: Multiple White House staffers are using computers equipped with residential proxy services that make their internet addresses available for commercial rental to third parties. One proxy service is operated by a Russian company whose hosting infrastructure was previously used as ground zero for cyberattacks against U.S. election systems.

cybersecurity.title: Cursor Confirms Security Breach Led to Malicious Claude Code Extension
cybersecurity.summary: The AI development platform Cursor suffered a security breach that allowed attackers to distribute a malicious Claude Code extension through its marketplace after stealing credentials from infrastructure provider Fireworks AI. The compromise exposed users to code execution risks through a trusted marketplace channel.

cybersecurity.title: Attackers Exploit UnrealIRCd Flaw That Enables Server-Level Command Injection
cybersecurity.summary: CISA added a high-severity vulnerability in UnrealIRCd to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog following reports of active in-the-wild exploitation. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-114713 with a CVSS score of 8.6, allows improper neutralization of delimiters leading to command injection attacks.

cybersecurity.title: German Military Drone Operations Disrupted by Cyberattack
cybersecurity.summary: German defense technology company Quantum Systems confirmed detection of a cyberattack in late October by hostile actors that disrupted military drone operations. The incident underscores vulnerabilities in critical defense infrastructure and ongoing threats to military capabilities.

cybersecurity.title: Attackers in Binance Breach Targeted Known Weakness, Missing Controls
cybersecurity.summary: The Binance breach exploited known weaknesses in blockchain security architecture and absent compensating controls designed to limit damage from exchange compromises. Attackers leveraged sophisticated techniques including deploying sweepers to circumvent protective measures.

health-biotech.title: The FDA has over 1k open jobs — and the staffing shortage is hitting pharma
health-biotech.summary: The FDA continues to struggle with significant staffing shortages following a mass exodus last year, with over 1,000 open positions affecting drug review timelines and industry operations. The agency's inability to fill these positions is creating bottlenecks that directly impact pharmaceutical companies' ability to advance their development programs and obtain regulatory approvals.

health-biotech.title: HHS plans funding for research into ibogaine for PTSD
health-biotech.summary: The Trump administration will allocate up to $4.9 million in federal funding to support clinical research into ibogaine, a psychedelic compound, as a potential treatment for post-traumatic stress disorder and addiction disorders. This funding signals growing government interest in novel psychedelic-based therapeutics for mental health conditions.

health-biotech.title: Blackstone bets $1.5B on Pfizer's obesity drug
health-biotech.summary: Blackstone has committed $1.5 billion to support a large Phase 3 clinical program for Pfizer's monthly GLP-1 injection candidate for obesity, which Pfizer obtained through a competitive acquisition of the previous developer, Metsera. The substantial investment underscores the significant commercial opportunity in the obesity treatment market.

health-biotech.title: Doctors have questions about the Watchman. Boston Scientific has a sales pitch.
health-biotech.summary: An investigation by the Boston Globe examines whether Boston Scientific's marketing practices for its Watchman cardiac implant have outpaced the clinical evidence supporting its use. The report raises questions about the alignment between promotional claims and scientific data for this widely marketed device.

health-biotech.title: Senators introduce bill to curb conflicts of interest on preventive care panel
health-biotech.summary: U.S. senators have introduced legislation to address financial conflicts of interest among members of the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force, a panel whose recommendations shape clinical guidelines and policy. The effort follows STAT reporting revealing that some panel members could financially benefit from their recommendations.

health-biotech.title: Democrats coalesce around 'Medicare for More,' 'Medikids' proposals
health-biotech.summary: Democratic lawmakers are rallying behind healthcare reform proposals that would expand Medicare coverage to more Americans, with initiatives such as 'Medicare for More' and 'Medikids' gaining consensus among party members. These proposals represent a significant shift in the party's healthcare policy approach.

health-biotech.title: Drug price hikes in Germany could push US costs higher, study says
health-biotech.summary: A new study warns that escalating drug prices in Germany may have spillover effects on U.S. pharmaceutical costs, amid growing tensions between the two countries over pricing policies. Several major pharmaceutical companies have responded to the pricing pressure by reducing their investment commitments in Germany.

health-biotech.title: This week in charts: Brain drugs are back on venture capitalists' minds
health-biotech.summary: Five neurology-focused biotech startups have collectively raised approximately $450 million in recent weeks, signaling renewed venture capital interest in central nervous system drug development. In contrast, investors have shown more subdued enthusiasm for the latest cell therapy research.

health-biotech.title: Bristol Myers research chief to depart in 'evolution' of company's structure
health-biotech.summary: Robert Plenge is departing from his role as research chief at Bristol Myers Squibb as part of a strategic reorganization that will consolidate the company's R&D operations. The restructuring aims to accelerate drug development timelines and better leverage emerging technologies.

health-biotech.title: AstraZeneca pulls EU filing for antibody as CHMP backs Gazyvaro in lupus
health-biotech.summary: AstraZeneca has withdrawn its European Union marketing application for a monoclonal antibody candidate in amyloidosis patients following previous late-stage study failures, while the Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use has backed the approval of Gazyvaro for lupus treatment. The company's decision reflects a strategic reassessment of its antibody program in the broader patient population.

startups-vc.title: With $720M round, Britain's Fractile gets a leg up in the race for AI chips
startups-vc.summary: Fractile has secured a $720 million funding round, establishing itself as one of the top-funded players in the competitive market for purpose-built AI chips. The substantial capital injection positions the British startup to accelerate development and deployment of specialized semiconductor technology.

startups-vc.title: SaaStr AI App of the Week: SciFin. The Nutanix and Cohesity Founder Raised $44 Million to Build AI for Sales Teams.
startups-vc.summary: SciFin, founded by a veteran entrepreneur from Nutanix and Cohesity, has raised $44 million to develop AI tools that address pipeline visibility and forecasting challenges in sales organizations. The platform aims to reduce time spent on deal updates and enable sales teams to focus on actual selling rather than administrative tasks.

startups-vc.title: Exclusive: Nubank Alum Raises $14M For Colombia's Palomma To Tackle Rent Payments, Landlord Financing
startups-vc.summary: Colombia-based fintech startup Palomma, founded by a Nubank alumnus, has raised $10 million in Series A funding led by Mexican venture firm Cometa to expand its financial services platform serving landlords, tenants, and property managers. The funding accelerates the company's growth in Latin America's rental and property management finance sector.

startups-vc.title: 5 Interesting Learnings from Palantir at $9.3 Billion Run-Rate: 96% Growth, 165% NRR, and U.S. Commercial Passing Government for the First Time
startups-vc.summary: Palantir reported Q3 results showing 96% year-over-year revenue growth and a $9.3 billion run rate, with quarterly revenue surpassing $2 billion for the first time and U.S. commercial revenues overtaking government contracts. The company's strong net revenue retention of 165% demonstrates sustained customer expansion despite stock market headwinds.

startups-vc.title: Our AI VP of Revenue Can't Close a Deal Yet. But It Co-Closed Two Six-Figure Deals in One Week.
startups-vc.summary: AI-powered sales agents have advanced beyond SDR and support functions to successfully co-close significant six-figure deals, though fully autonomous account executive capabilities remain unrealized. The progress demonstrates the expanding role of AI in enterprise sales processes while highlighting the remaining gap in closing complex deals.

startups-vc.title: VCs Are Still Chasing Protein, Even As Fake Meat Falls Out Of Favor
startups-vc.summary: Venture capital investment in the protein sector has shifted away from meat substitutes toward protein-enriched packaged foods and beverages across various categories including noodles, cereals, and snacks. This strategic pivot reflects changing consumer preferences and market dynamics within the competitive food and beverage startup ecosystem.

startups-vc.title: Startup Founders Are Using AI To File Patents. Here's Where DIY Becomes A Liability.
startups-vc.summary: While AI can reduce patent preparation costs for startups, DIY patent applications risk overlooking critical issues that could jeopardize investor confidence and competitive positioning. Legal experts argue that combining AI tools with professional legal expertise delivers more commercially valuable patent protection that withstands investor scrutiny.

startups-vc.title: Phota Labs uses AI to turn everyday photos into professional-looking shots
startups-vc.summary: Phota Labs is developing AI-powered tools to automate photo editing, enabling consumers to transform casual moments into polished images without manual intervention or technical expertise. The startup aims to address the consumer photography market by simplifying the editing process through advanced artificial intelligence.

startups-vc.title: How Yair Alon went from building Portrait Mode at Google to founding researcher at Poetiq
startups-vc.summary: Yair Alon, a veteran Google Research and DeepMind engineer with 10 years of experience in AI development, has joined Y Combinator-backed Poetiq as a founding researcher to build self-improving AI systems. His transition reflects the movement of senior AI talent from established tech companies to emerging startups pursuing frontier AI capabilities.

startups-vc.title: $1 Billion ARR Is the New $100 Million. The Public B2B Companies Below It Show Why.
startups-vc.summary: The threshold for strategic insulation in B2B software has shifted from $100 million to $1 billion ARR, as public company analysis reveals the competitive advantages and durability gains available only at higher revenue scales. The shift reflects increased capital efficiency requirements and market consolidation pressures in enterprise software.

crypto-web3.title: Bitcoin crashes to 3-month low below $63,000 as analyst flags fourth capitulation wave
crypto-web3.summary: Bitcoin has declined to its lowest level in three months, falling below $63,000 amid signs of investor capitulation in the market. Analysts observe that investors are now selling at price points they regretted missing three months prior, suggesting potential market exhaustion.

crypto-web3.title: Bitcoin ETFs lose $1 billion for the second week in a row as crypto funds, except one, continue bleeding
crypto-web3.summary: U.S. spot cryptocurrency ETFs experienced a second consecutive week of outflows, totaling approximately $1.55 billion in combined losses across 15 tracked categories. The sustained redemptions reflect broader weakness in institutional crypto investment demand.

crypto-web3.title: XRP crashes to its lowest since November 2024 as money leaves crypto
crypto-web3.summary: Ripple's XRP token has declined to its lowest price since November 2024, driven by ETF outflows and declining stablecoin supplies exerting downward pressure across cryptocurrency markets. The asset's weakness reflects broader fund redemptions and reduced liquidity conditions.

crypto-web3.title: Kava Lend loses roughly $3.8 million to hack, sending KAVA token down nearly 40%
crypto-web3.summary: The Kava Lend protocol suffered a security breach resulting in approximately $3.8 million in losses, with attackers bridging roughly 49.2 million KAVA tokens to BNB Chain and liquidating them for $2.1 million in stablecoins and other assets. The incident triggered a sharp 40% decline in the KAVA token's market value.

crypto-web3.title: UK, Singapore, and Thailand central banks test cross-border FX settlement as stablecoins gain ground
crypto-web3.summary: Project Meridian FX APAC demonstrated successful coordination of foreign exchange transactions across both traditional settlement systems and blockchain-based infrastructure, signaling central bank progress toward cross-border digital payment integration. The initiative underscores growing acceptance of blockchain technology for official monetary settlement processes.

crypto-web3.title: Kazakhstan plans tokenized government bonds in first quarter after $22 million note sale
crypto-web3.summary: Kazakhstan announced plans to issue tokenized government bonds in the first quarter, building upon its successful sale of $22 million in tokenized central bank notes. The initiative reflects the country's commitment to expanding blockchain adoption within its domestic financial infrastructure.

crypto-web3.title: Britain could turn wasted Scottish wind power into bitcoin to cut its $1.3 billion grid bill
crypto-web3.summary: A Bitcoin Policy Institute report suggests Britain could utilize surplus Scottish wind power generation for bitcoin mining to reduce the approximately $1.3 billion in annual grid payments made to wind farms for halting production. The strategy would convert otherwise wasted renewable energy into economic value while addressing grid management costs.

crypto-web3.title: House Oversight Chair calls for possible ban on government officials' prediction market bets over insider trading concerns
crypto-web3.summary: The House Oversight Committee has proposed new restrictions on government officials' participation in prediction markets, including a potential outright ban, citing insider trading risks and conflicts of interest. The initiative addresses concerns that public officials could leverage non-public information for financial gain through event-based betting platforms.

crypto-web3.title: Ethereum scaling project MegaETH slashes staff by 20% as it pursues AI business
crypto-web3.summary: The Ethereum scaling project MegaETH announced a 20% workforce reduction as it pivots its strategy toward artificial intelligence applications, coinciding with a significant decline in protocol-based decentralized finance value from $245 million to $8.8 million. The restructuring reflects the protocol's strategic reorientation away from core DeFi operations.

crypto-web3.title: A behind the scenes force may amplify bitcoin and ether price volatility
crypto-web3.summary: Market analysis indicates that both bitcoin and ether are trading within price ranges where market makers and dealers may contribute to increased price volatility through their trading activities. The positioning of these assets suggests structural factors could exacerbate price swings in the near term.

energy-climate.title: Analysis: Climate-finance pledges fall 70% as countries meet at COP31
energy-climate.summary: Public funding pledged to developing countries for climate action has declined by more than 70% during COP31 negotiations in Antalya, Turkey. This significant reduction threatens climate mitigation and adaptation efforts in vulnerable nations.

energy-climate.title: Analysis: China's quarterly CO2 falls 3% in largest drop since Covid
energy-climate.summary: China's carbon dioxide emissions declined by 3.1% in the third quarter of 2026, marking the largest quarterly reduction since the COVID-19 pandemic as the Hormuz crisis continued. This emissions trend reflects significant shifts in China's energy and economic patterns.

energy-climate.title: What's next for California's climate laws following an appeals court split decision
energy-climate.summary: The Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals upheld scope 1 and scope 2 emissions reporting under California's SB 253 while blocking enforcement of scope 3 reporting and SB 261. The split ruling creates uncertainty for California's comprehensive climate disclosure framework.

energy-climate.title: Masdar completes $950 million solar and battery storage project in California
energy-climate.summary: Abu Dhabi's Masdar and joint venture partner Terra-Gen have brought the Lockhart complex online, adding 365 MW of solar capacity and 173.7 MW of energy storage to the California grid. The $950 million project represents significant investment in utility-scale renewable energy infrastructure.

energy-climate.title: NRG to sell six natural gas assets to LS Power for $4bn
energy-climate.summary: NRG Energy has agreed to divest six natural gas generation assets to LS Power for $4 billion in cash, signaling continued restructuring within the energy sector. The transaction reflects ongoing market shifts as utilities reallocate capital toward renewable energy.

energy-climate.title: Renewables to exceed 80% of Netherlands' power capacity by 2035, says GlobalData
energy-climate.summary: The Netherlands is projected to reach renewable energy capacity exceeding 80% of total power generation by 2035, with the transition shifting from rooftop solar to offshore wind and grid flexibility solutions due to congestion concerns. Negative midday pricing is pushing utilities toward dispatchable renewable technologies.

energy-climate.title: SSEN Transmission breaks ground on Lewis Hub electricity project
energy-climate.summary: SSEN Transmission has commenced construction on the Lewis Hub, which will establish the Western Isles' first direct electricity transmission connection to mainland Great Britain. The project is essential for integrating renewable energy resources from Scotland's remote regions.

energy-climate.title: UNSW develops three-minute lithium-ion battery health test
energy-climate.summary: Researchers at the University of New South Wales have created a prototype using electrical pulses and statistical models to assess lithium-ion battery health in under three minutes per cell. The technology has potential applications for sorting and optimizing the reuse and recycling of battery storage systems.

energy-climate.title: Shinsung E&G unveils 650 W bifacial TOPCon solar modules with 23.25% efficiency
energy-climate.summary: South Korean manufacturer Shinsung E&G has launched next-generation n-type TOPCon bifacial solar modules with power outputs up to 650 W and conversion efficiencies of 23.25%. The modules target ground-mounted, floating, and agrivoltaic applications.

energy-climate.title: Clarifying the CATL Tener Sodium, with new specifications and availability
energy-climate.summary: CATL has released updated specifications for its Tener sodium-ion battery system, positioning the product as a cost-competitive alternative to lithium iron phosphate batteries. International deliveries are scheduled to begin in summer 2027, expanding battery technology options for energy storage applications.

asia-pacific.title: Asean's neutrality set to be tested as Philippines welcomes world leaders
asia-pacific.summary: World leaders including US President Donald Trump, Chinese Premier Li Qiang, and other senior officials are converging in Manila for the Asean summit, highlighting the 11-member bloc's growing geopolitical significance with a 700 million population and $4.4 trillion economy expected to become the world's fourth largest by 2030. The summit will test Asean's traditional neutrality amid rising great power competition in the region.

asia-pacific.title: Malaysia's Melaka poll shows ethnic lines firming. Can Anwar turn Malay nationalist tide?
asia-pacific.summary: Malaysia's recent state elections demonstrate a troubling consolidation of voting patterns along ethnic lines, undermining Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim's multicultural ruling coalition in its third consecutive electoral defeat this year. Identity politics is emerging as a decisive factor that could determine the outcome of Malaysia's next national election.

asia-pacific.title: Hong Kong sending who's who delegation of business leaders to Apec CEO Summit
asia-pacific.summary: Hong Kong is dispatching one of its largest-ever delegations, comprising at least 54 senior business leaders, executives, and representatives from major chambers and banks to the Apec CEO Summit in Shenzhen. The delegation's participation underscores Hong Kong's continued efforts to leverage regional economic integration within the Greater Bay Area framework.

asia-pacific.title: UBS unveils new West Kowloon hub to tap Greater Bay Area wealth
asia-pacific.summary: UBS has opened its new Hong Kong headquarters in West Kowloon, a 20-storey tower designed to consolidate its regional operations and serve as a wealth management hub for the Greater Bay Area. The move reflects major financial institutions' strategic pivot to tap expanding wealth pools across mainland China's key economic zones.

asia-pacific.title: Can Chinese AI companies curb cyber risks from open-weight models without losing their edge?
asia-pacific.summary: Major Chinese AI firms including Tencent and Moonshot AI are voluntarily restricting the cybersecurity capabilities of their advanced open-weight models following high-profile AI hacking incidents affecting both US and Chinese companies. This regulatory response highlights growing tensions between advancing AI capabilities and managing emerging cybersecurity vulnerabilities in the competitive AI landscape.

asia-pacific.title: Chinese social media firms under fire as fake history spreads online
asia-pacific.summary: Chinese authorities report that pseudo-historical misinformation is proliferating across social media platforms due to algorithmic amplification, AI-generated content, and insufficient content monitoring. The phenomenon reflects broader concerns about information integrity and state capacity to manage narrative control on major digital platforms.

asia-pacific.title: Top tax accountant exam scorer in South Korea admits to using AI to cheat
asia-pacific.summary: South Korea's highest-scoring candidate in the recent tax accountant qualification examination admitted to using generative AI and camera technology to cheat after public scrutiny of his unusually high marks. The incident highlights emerging challenges in educational integrity and examination oversight amid rapid AI proliferation.

asia-pacific.title: Japan's AZEC and POWERR Asia Are Failing Southeast Asia
asia-pacific.summary: Japan's regional trade initiatives AZEC and POWERR Asia are criticized for conflating Japan's domestic fossil fuel strategy with regional decarbonization partnerships, failing to deliver genuine benefits to Southeast Asian partners. The analysis raises questions about the alignment between Japan's climate commitments and actual regional energy cooperation frameworks.

asia-pacific.title: North Korea's Last Defectors
asia-pacific.summary: Defections from North Korea are declining significantly, allowing leader Kim Jong Un to exert greater control over the country's international image and narrative. The reduced outflow of refugees constrains external access to information about conditions within North Korea.

asia-pacific.title: AI 'blue aliens' rising as health experts on China social media spark pseudoscience backlash
asia-pacific.summary: AI-generated digital entities depicted as alien emissaries are gaining traction on Chinese social media platforms, particularly on Douyin, spreading health misinformation and pseudoscience to millions of followers. The trend exemplifies challenges in managing AI-generated content credibility and misleading health advice on major platforms.
